summaryEn: A century-old Taiwanese paper pioneer turned investment-holding company — whose paper business loses money operationally, while virtually all its profit comes from investments, above all its crown-jewel stake in E Ink, the global e-paper leader it founded. A deep discount-to-book holding play with a long bio-materials/green transformation.
model: editorial (truth-audited: FinMind + Wikipedia/YFY/press; paper-holding framing — paper core stated bluntly as operationally loss-making (op margin negative) with profit from non-operating/equity-method income (E Ink), the 0.57x book discount and transformation credited; FY2025 op-loss/pretax-profit confirmed by company; sector/nameZh/listedYear fixed)

sections.bodyMarkdown:
YFY Inc. (永豐餘投控, TWSE: 1907) is a **century-old Taiwanese paper pioneer that has become an investment-holding company** — and it is best understood not as a paper maker, but as a **discounted holding company** sitting on a valuable portfolio. Founded in **1924** (a He-family trading house) and the maker of Taiwan's **first private paper** in 1950, it **listed in 1977** and **reorganized into a holding company in 2012**. Critically, in **1992 it founded E Ink (元太, TPEx: 8069)** — today the **global leader in electronic paper** — which remains its **crown-jewel affiliate**.

The honest core fact, confirmed by both FinMind and the company's own figures, is striking: **the paper business loses money at the operating level, and virtually all of YFY's profit comes from non-operating income — above all equity-method earnings from E Ink and other affiliates.** In 2026Q1 the **operating margin was −0.43%** (an operating *loss*, consistent with negative operating margins right through 2024–2025), yet the **net margin was +1.43%**. For FY2025 the company reported **revenue ~NT$73.6bn, an operating loss of ~NT$831m, but a pretax profit of ~NT$2.69bn** — the entire profit, and more, came from **investment income**. **ROE is just ~2.7%.**

That is why the market values it as a holding company, not an operator: the stock trades at a remarkable **~0.57× book value** — a deep discount to its ~NT$95bn of equity. The investment case is therefore a **sum-of-the-parts / deep-value** one: the **E Ink stake** and other investments, the **paper subsidiary (China Paper Pulp, 中華紙漿)**, and a long **transformation into bio-materials, circular economy, green energy and specialty fiber** ("paper is not just paper," in chairman Ho Shou-chuan's framing). Two-sided: **deep book discount + a valuable E Ink stake + green-transformation optionality + a century of heritage + a dividend** — against an **operationally loss-making core, very low ROE, lumpy investment-dependent profit, and a complex holding structure.**

YFY is one of Taiwan's **oldest industrial lineages**. In **1924**, the **He brothers (何傳, 何永, 何義)** opened a trading house in **Anping, Tainan**, in their father's name — the seed of what became the **Yuen Foong Yu (永豐餘) group**. In **1950** they established **Yuen Foong Yu Paper — Taiwan's first privately-owned paper company** — and built it into one of the island's paper champions, listing on the **Taiwan Stock Exchange in 1977**.

But paper is a **mature, cyclical, capital-heavy commodity**, and over the decades the economics deteriorated (Chinese oversupply, the digital decline of graphic paper, volatile pulp and FX). YFY's response was **diversification and transformation** — and its single best decision was founding **E Ink (元太) in 1992**, originally a TFT-LCD venture that, after acquiring the US E Ink Corporation's MIT-born electronic-ink technology in 2009, became the **global monopoly-like leader in e-paper** (e-readers, electronic shelf labels). E Ink grew into a far more valuable business than YFY's paper operations.

In **2012**, Yuen Foong Yu Paper reorganized into **YFY Inc. (永豐餘投資控股)** — a **holding company** spanning paper, technology (E Ink), bio-materials, green energy and more. Under chairman **Ho Shou-chuan (何壽川)**, its modern identity is a **"paper is not just paper" transformation** — turning a declining commodity base into **specialty fiber, bio-materials and circular-economy** businesses, while its investment portfolio (led by E Ink) carries the value.

- **1924** — The **He brothers** open a trading house in **Tainan** — the group's origin.
- **1950** — Establish **Yuen Foong Yu Paper** — **Taiwan's first private paper company**.
- **1977** — **Lists on the Taiwan Stock Exchange (1907)**.
- **1992** — **Founds E Ink (元太)** — later the **global e-paper leader** (after acquiring US E Ink's tech in 2009).
- **2012** — Reorganizes into **YFY Inc. (永豐餘投資控股)** — a holding company across paper, tech, bio-materials, green energy.
- **2010s–2020s** — Pushes **"paper is not just paper"** transformation (bio-materials, zero-plastic, circular economy); paper subsidiary **China Paper Pulp (中華紙漿)** sets up fiber/specialty-materials divisions.
- **FY2025** — Revenue ~NT$73.6bn, **operating loss ~NT$831m, but pretax profit ~NT$2.69bn** (investment income); EPS NT$1.19, dividend NT$1.0.

YFY's finances only make sense once you read it as a **holding company**, not a paper operator.

- **Profit comes from investments, not operations.** The paper core runs an **operating loss** (operating margin −0.43% in 2026Q1, negative through 2024–2025), yet the company is net-profitable because of **non-operating / equity-method income** — overwhelmingly its **E Ink stake** and other affiliates. FY2025 made this explicit: an **operating loss of ~NT$831m** but a **pretax profit of ~NT$2.69bn**.
- **A deep discount to book.** The stock trades at **~0.57× book value** — the market values ~NT$95bn of equity at roughly NT$54bn. This is the classic **holding-company discount**, compounded by the loss-making core — but it also means the **E Ink and other investments may be worth more than the price implies** (the deep-value angle).
- **A moderate balance sheet.** A **~46% debt ratio** on ~NT$178bn of assets, against ~NT$95bn of equity and ~NT$10bn of cash — manageable for a capital-heavy paper/materials base.
- **A dividend funded by investment income.** Cash dividends have run **NT$0.8–1.5** in recent years (NT$1.0 for FY2025), supported by **dividends received from affiliates** rather than paper profits — a ~3.7% yield.

The financing reality: a **deep-discount holding company** whose reported profit and dividend are **carried by its investment portfolio (E Ink above all)**, while the operating paper business is a cyclical drag — so the balance-sheet question is about **NAV and the value of the stakes**, not operating cash generation.

**Stance: a deep-discount holding company whose value rests on its investment portfolio — above all E Ink — not on its loss-making paper operations. A sum-of-the-parts / deep-value play with green-transformation optionality, for patient, NAV-minded investors.**

The bull case:

1. **A deep discount to book.** At **~0.57× book**, the market heavily discounts ~NT$95bn of equity — potentially undervaluing the stakes within.
2. **A crown-jewel investment.** YFY founded and holds a significant stake in **E Ink (元太)** — the **global e-paper leader**, a high-quality, growing, monopoly-like business worth far more than YFY's paper operations.
3. **Transformation optionality + dividend.** A genuine push into **bio-materials, circular economy, green energy and specialty fiber**, a century of heritage, and a **~3.7% dividend** (funded by investment income).

The counter-arguments are central:

- **The core loses money operationally.** Paper runs an operating loss (op margin negative); **ROE is just ~2.7%** — the operating business destroys, not creates, value.
- **Lumpy, investment-dependent profit.** Earnings swing with **equity-method income** (E Ink's results, disposal gains), not steady operations — EPS bounces (NT$0.98–1.31) and quarters are uneven.
- **Holding-company opacity and discount.** Complex structure; the **book discount can persist** for years if the market keeps penalizing the loss-making core.
- **Transformation is early and capital-heavy.** Bio-materials/green is aspirational against a declining, capital-intensive paper base.

A **deep-value / NAV** thesis: you are buying a discounted portfolio (chiefly E Ink) wrapped around a weak operating business — attractive if the discount closes or the stakes are revalued, frustrating if neither happens.

YFY earns its returns in two very different ways — and only one of them actually makes money right now:

- **The operating businesses (paper & materials) — currently a drag.** Through subsidiaries (notably **China Paper Pulp / 中華紙漿**) it makes **industrial paper, paperboard, pulp and packaging** — a **mature, cyclical commodity** with thin gross margins (~13%) and, lately, **operating losses** (Chinese oversupply, the digital decline of paper, volatile pulp/FX). The transformation push — **specialty fiber, bio-materials, zero-plastic packaging, circular economy, green energy and industrial gas** — aims to turn this base into higher-value materials, but it is **early and capital-heavy**.
- **The investment portfolio — where the profit is.** As a **holding company**, YFY's real earnings engine is **equity-method and investment income** from affiliates — **above all E Ink (元太)**, the global e-paper leader it founded, plus other tech/financial/consumer holdings. This is why **net profit exists despite an operating loss**, and why the stock is valued on **sum-of-the-parts / NAV** rather than operating multiples.

The economic logic: YFY is essentially a **diversified holding vehicle** whose paper roots are being reinvented while its **investment stakes carry the value**. The levers are: **the value and earnings of E Ink and other stakes**, the **success of the bio-materials/green transformation**, the **paper cycle** (whether the core can stop bleeding), and **whether the deep book discount narrows**. The key honest point — visible in the negative operating margin — is that **the paper business does not earn the profit; the investments do.**

YFY sits at the intersection of two very different worlds, which is exactly why it is hard to value as one thing:

- **Paper & packaging (a declining/cyclical commodity).** Graphic paper is in **secular digital decline**; industrial paper/packaging is **cyclical and oversupplied** (especially by China), with thin margins and volatile pulp and energy costs. Taiwanese peers include **Cheng Loong (正隆)** and **Longchen**; the global industry is consolidating and pivoting to packaging and specialty. This is a **tough, low-return** arena — hence YFY's operating losses and its transformation urgency.
- **Specialty materials / circular economy (the pivot).** Bio-based materials, **molded-fiber/zero-plastic packaging**, nano-cellulose, recycling and green energy — a **growing, higher-value** space where YFY (via China Paper Pulp) is repositioning. Competitive, early, and capital-intensive, but with a sustainability tailwind.
- **The investment dimension (the value).** Through **E Ink (元太)**, YFY has exposure to a **genuinely world-class, monopoly-like technology business** — e-paper for e-readers and the fast-growing **electronic-shelf-label (ESL)** market, where E Ink dominates globally. This stake's value and growth dwarf the paper operations.

The competitive truth framing YFY: **the paper business competes in a tough, declining commodity; the transformation is promising but unproven; and the real differentiator is the investment portfolio (E Ink) — a holding-company structure where the parts are worth more than the operating whole, if the market ever credits them.**

**Strengths**
- A **deep discount to book (~0.57× P/B)** on ~NT$95bn equity — potential hidden value.
- A **crown-jewel stake in E Ink (元太)**, the global e-paper leader YFY founded — high-quality, growing.
- Century-old heritage; a genuine **bio-materials/circular-economy transformation**; ~3.7% dividend.

**Weaknesses**
- **Paper core is operationally loss-making** (op margin negative); **ROE just ~2.7%**.
- **Lumpy, investment-dependent profit** (equity-method income, not steady operations).
- **Complex, opaque holding structure**; the book discount can persist.

**Opportunities**
- Re-rating if the book discount narrows or the stakes (E Ink) are revalued/monetized.
- Bio-materials, **zero-plastic/molded-fiber packaging**, circular economy and green-energy growth.
- E Ink's ESL/e-paper expansion lifting equity-method income.

**Threats**
- Secular decline of paper; Chinese oversupply; pulp/FX/energy cost swings deepening operating losses.
- Capital-heavy, early transformation that may not pay off.
- Dependence on E Ink's results; persistent holding-company discount.

- **Operationally loss-making core.** The paper business runs an operating loss (op margin −0.43% in 2026Q1, negative through 2024–2025); without an operating turnaround, the company depends entirely on investment income.
- **Investment-dependent, lumpy profit.** Net profit comes from **equity-method income (E Ink and affiliates)** and disposal gains — uneven and outside management's day-to-day control; a weak year at E Ink would hit YFY directly.
- **Persistent holding-company discount.** The ~0.57× book discount may **not close** — markets can penalize complex holding structures and loss-making cores for years.
- **Paper-industry decline.** Secular digital decline, Chinese oversupply, and volatile pulp/FX/energy costs pressure the core.
- **Transformation execution.** Bio-materials/green/specialty-fiber is **early and capital-heavy**; returns are unproven, and it competes against established players.
- **Capital intensity / cyclicality.** An asset-heavy old-economy base ties up capital at low returns (ROE ~2.7%).

YFY's path is a **deep-value, NAV-driven story**: whether its investment value gets recognized and whether its transformation can fix the operating core. The axes to watch:

- **E Ink and the portfolio.** The single biggest value driver — E Ink's e-paper/ESL growth and earnings (which flow into YFY's profit), and whether any stakes are revalued or monetized in a way that narrows the **0.57× book discount**.
- **The paper turnaround.** Whether the core can stop running **operating losses** — via specialty/bio-materials mix, capacity rationalization, and cost discipline — or remains a cyclical drag.
- **The transformation.** Progress in **bio-materials, zero-plastic/molded-fiber packaging, circular economy and green energy** — converting "paper is not just paper" into real, profitable revenue.
- **Capital return.** Sustaining the dividend (funded by investment income) through the cycle.

Bottom line: YFY is a **deep-discount holding company** whose **value rests on its investment portfolio — above all E Ink — not on its operationally loss-making paper business**. It offers a **sum-of-the-parts / NAV** opportunity (0.57× book, a world-class e-paper stake, green optionality) wrapped around a **weak, capital-heavy core (ROE ~2.7%)** with **lumpy, investment-dependent earnings**. Judge it on **the value of its stakes, the closing (or not) of the book discount, and a paper/transformation turnaround** — and value it as the holding company it is, not the paper maker it used to be.
